4733.title: Een moeder die haar kind pap voert
4733.creator: Unknown

editorial.note: Een moeder die haar kind pap voert. Een zittende vrouw voert met een lepel uit een aardewerken kom pap aan een staand kind.

Een jonge vrouw speelt, in een voornaam interieur, op het virginaal. Op het deksel van het instrument is een landschap geschilderd met een intiem wandelend stelletje. Muziek brengt mensen samen – nodigt de muzikante uit om mee te spelen?

editorial.note: Bakker Korff’s usual somewhat caustic humour is absent here. The woman making waffles is painted with just as much attention as the copper pans behind her, or the marble floor on which she sits.
Ter Borch probably depicted his half-sister Gesina ter Borch here. She, too, was an artist, and frequently modelled for him.

In 1663, the plague ravaged Amsterdam, claiming one in ten lives. Around this time, Metsu painted this picture of a mother comforting her sick child. Their posture evokes a pieta: the Virgin Mary with the body of Jesus on her lap.

148312.creator: Adriaen Brouwer

source.institution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Open Access

editorial.note: Oil on wood. European Paintings.
A maidservant pours milk, entirely absorbed in her work. Except for the stream of milk, everything else is still.
The woman is depicted as an industrious, virtuous housewife. The basket on the wall holds the yarn she has already spun.
Seated at a table in a run-down interior, an elderly man and a young woman pray before their meal.

152080.title: Old Woman Saying Grace, Known as ‘The Prayer without End’
152080.creator: Nicolaes Maes

editorial.note: An old woman prays devoutly before eating her meal. She does not let the begging cat tugging impatiently on the tablecloth distract her. The virtue of the old woman lies in her self-control and sense of duty to God.

152081.title: Woman Eating, Known as ‘The Cat’s Breakfast’
152081.creator: Gabriël Metsu

editorial.note: A woman of humble origin shares her meal with a cat. In the 17th century it was not unusual to consume herring with bread (and beer!) for breakfast.
A young woman, the painter’s wife, drinks coffee, a popular beverage in the 18th century.

152120.title: Interior with a Mother Combing Her Child’s Hair, Known as ‘Maternal Care’
152120.creator: Caspar Netscher

editorial.note: These two children serve as examples of good and bad upbringing. Toys litter the floor in a dimly lit bedroom. A mother combs the long curls of her son, who obediently leans on her lap.

Has the baby fallen asleep yet? A woman carefully lifts the cloth draped over the cradle. Her book of verses rests in her lap. The fall of light and warm red hues of the blanket draw attention to the woman with her child.

152358.title: Man and Woman at the Breakfast Table
152358.creator: Gabriël Metsu

editorial.note: On the table is a plate with a ham, cheese, and bread. For the average family, this was a typical breakfast, sometimes supplemented by fish. The woman is about to pour some beer into her flute glass.
